newsitem.title: PERU: Peru govt rejects rebel counterproposal on talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru govt rejects rebel counterproposal on talks.

text.p: Peru said on Thursday it had rejected a proposal by Marxist rebels holding 74 hostages that the Guatemalan government take part in talks to end the 30-day stand-off.

"The Peruvian government does not accept the proposal that a representative of the Guatemalan government take part in the commission," Peruvian government negotiator Domingo Palermo told a news conference.
The government considered that trying to bring Guatemala into the talks was an effort by the rebels to suggest a similarity between the recently-ended civil war there and the situation in Peru.
"With this suggestion the aim is to establish an analogy with a completely different reality," Palermo said.
He also said that Red Cross visits to Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement rebels held in Peruvian jails were being suspended "in order to avoid disturbing the process of talks."

The government was evaluating the rest of the rebel proposal, which included the participation of an unnamed European country in the talks. Palermo did not say whether the government accepted that suggestion.
